cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x102452, with supervise resolving `expect wsh_read_probe 0x102442` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner layer between -- wiretap, wsutil and ui do not use wmem, and epan/uat.c and epan/charsets.c take the crossed buffer from g_malloc or from the caller -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: `memcmp` is SPECIFIED to read n bytes from both operands regardless of content, so the defect exists even where a byte-wise implementation would stop early at the in-bounds terminator -- which is exactly why the fix switches to `strncmp`, whose contract stops at a terminator. A detector keyed on what the implementation happens to touch and one keyed on the contract disagree here, and ASan's interceptor follows the contract.
